John, Kate, Jack, Luke—would you each agree to catch 12 tons this month instead of 10? I’m offering to take the same 12-ton limit myself. Each of us would earn $12,000 rather than $10,000: an extra $2,000 each, or $10,000 across the group.

With everyone at 12, we’d catch 60 tons and leave 40. That keeps us above the 5-ton collapse threshold this month. Next month’s stock would be 100 tons with 75% probability and 80 tons with 25% probability—not guaranteed recovery. By comparison, everyone taking 10 leaves 50, which becomes 100 under either recovery outcome.

So 12 gives us more income now but sacrifices that certain full stock next month. If we start next month at 80, repeating a 60-ton total catch would leave only 20; we should discuss catches again based on the stock then, rather than promise 12 forever. Any future restraint would remain voluntary, and this proposal depends on everyone sticking to the agreed total.

Luke, would you support this proposal and help discuss the tradeoff? John, Kate, and Jack, can each of you explicitly commit to 12 this month, or tell us what makes you hesitant? I’m willing to discuss a different whole-ton allocation if that would earn everyone’s agreement.
